newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Costello eyes internet tax avoidance.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello eyes internet tax avoidance.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday the government was concerned about the tax avoidance through the Internet.
"The Internet is one of those technological developments which does pose a threat to our current taxation base," Costello told reporters after launching a taxpayers' rights campaign.
Australian consumers currently can avoid sales tax and import duties by purchasing items such as electronic and sporting goods from internet vendors.
Costello said the fact that internet buyers could electronically locate transactions outside of the government's jurisdiction was a challenge to the tax base.
"We have had a a group within the tax office working on the challenges of the technology of globalisation for some time," Costello said.
Earlier this week, U.S. President Bill Clinton called for global free trade on the internet, a proposal which if adopted could lead to huge jump in internet commerce.
